rv.q: In essence THE MARK is a relevant and thoroughly entertaining show, an excellent vehicle for the special magic of the Babes w/Blades.
The Mark fulfills its mission, presenting the trickiest of balancing acts between action and moral quandary in a divided world.
Still, THE MARK leaves a battle scar. These Babes are tough.
Babes With Blades uses stage combat to tell stories that elevate the voices of the underrepresented and dismantle the patriarchy.

The second act was enjoyable enough just to see the increasingly absurd plot twists unraveled (just don’t think too much about the logic behind them and you’ll be fine), and the actors and the action sequences are great, but at least for me it was a letdown after Act I.

cn.t: Critics praise "The Mark" for its timely dystopian storytelling and thrilling combat choreography, with Babes With Blades delivering another excellent production featuring the company's signature stage combat expertise.
